messages:
Kayla Chen: Heads-up, canary shows a host-side decode + preparse tail bump after yesterday's kernel selector change. 95th latency for short requests jumped ~18%. attaching quick profile link: https://internal.prof/pprof/1799912345
Eddie Park: thanks, Kayla. is this on http2 or grpc ingress? any correlation with request size?
Kayla Chen: grpc primarily; most requests are <= 600 bytes input. CPU breakdown from the pprof: 45% tokenization/byte-scan, 20% proto-unpack, 12% stream framing, 8% syscall overhead, rest split across batching/kvcache plumbing
Ryan Mills: that tokenization % feels high compared to baseline. did kernel selection alter decode path (AVX path vs scalar) for small sequences?
Kayla Chen: yes — the selector now prefers kernel_v2 when avg_seq < 128 to improve throughput. suspecting v2 has worse microbehavior for tiny payloads that triggers extra parsing loop iterations
Mira Sol: noted. can you paste the minimal repro? i'll run perf and flamegraph on a devbox
Kayla Chen: repro (run against canary):
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do 
  curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/grpc' -d @payload_small.bin 
    "https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate" >/dev/null &
done
wait
```
Eddie Park: also try with `GRPC_ARG_HTTP2_WRITE_CB=true` and compare — we saw writev coalescing differences before that affected small writes
Mira Sol: running perf now. first glance: kernel_v2 entry adds an extra memcpy in host-proxy path + one extra conditional in the tokenizer loop. memcpy hot in `parse_slab()` when frames are >1 chunk
Kayla Chen: interesting — that matches the trace: stream chunker returns two slices more often under v2. might be preparse fragmentation heuristic triggering earlier fallback
Ryan Mills: could be batching heuristic interacts: with smaller sequences we dropped into microbatcher instead of noop, causing additional prefix handling. check `batch_hint` path in runtime config for canary (it was tightened last week)
Kayla Chen: confirmed: `batch_hint.max_fragments` was lowered from 8->4 in the rollout, which increases fragmenting. reverting to 8 on canary removes the majority of the extra memcpys and brings 95th down to ~6% over baseline instead of 18%
ingress-bot: deploy rollout event: kernel-selector:v2 -> canary (rollout id 2026-03-18-18)
Eddie Park: action items: 1) revert `batch_hint.max_fragments` on canary (done) 2) instrument tokenizer to expose fragment count metric 3) add a short-sequence fast-path in kernel_v2 to avoid extra memcpy 4) run replay on full traffic for 2 hours after revert
Mira Sol: I'll open a small PR to add fragment_count metric + p99 hist. Ryan, can you take the kernel_v2 micro-optim?
Ryan Mills: on it — i'll prototype branch that skips the extra slice copy when total length < 1024. will bench locally then send for review
Kayla Chen: thanks. let's hold the global rollout until we've verified kernel_v2 microfix + metrics. marking P1 regression in our tracker and pinging runtime oncall. :triangular_flag_on_post:
Eddie Park: once metrics land, i'll create dashboard with fragment_count, tokenizer_cpu, and grpc_writev_coalesce to watch during next canary run
Kayla Chen: perfect. if anyone finds quick wins in proto-unpack (we saw ~20% there too) flag it here. otherwise i'll follow up with timing notes and a short postmortem after we stabilize canary
Mira Sol: perf run finished: attaching flamegraph gist https://gist.internal/fg/1799912345 — tokenizer loop + parse_slab dominate. sending logs to the issue now
Kayla Chen: great, thanks everyone. I'll update the rollout ticket and add rollback timeline if we see >10% tail regression in prod. :thumbsup:
